## Installing packages 
```{r }

pkgs<-c("tidyverse", "readxl","writexl","haven","DBI")
```

## Loading packages
```{r }

## readr, dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr
library(tidyverse)

## excel files
library(readxl)

## SPSS, Stata, SAS files
library(haven)

## databases
library(DBI)

```

## Assignment 2
##Practicing the first class programs 
```{r }
### Data structure (Vectors, Factors, Lists, Data frame, matrix and arrays)
## Vector
## Numeric 
age<-c(20,25,39,30,32,25)
summary(age)
mean(age)
head(age)

## Logical
y<-c(TRUE,FALSE)
y<-c(T,F)

## Characters
x<-c("a","b","c","d")

## matrix
(x<-matrix(1:4, nrow =2, ncol =2  ))
(y<-matrix(1:6,nrow = 2,ncol = 3))

x%*%y

## List
(x<-list(TRUE,"a",5, 1+5i))

##Factor
x<-factor(c("yes","no","yes","yes"))


```

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
